label: Peaks
source: OS grid references converted to WGS84, each validated against SRTM 30m elevation; positions failing the height check were excluded.

items.title: Muncaster Fell
items.description: A 231m wooded ridge near the coast at the very start and end of the route.

items.title: Whin Rigg
items.description: The 535m southern end of the Wast Water Screes, above deep gullies.

items.title: Slight Side
items.description: The 762m southern outpost of Scafell, a rocky top on the long Eskdale approach.

items.title: Illgill Head
items.description: A 609m fell forming the top of the Wast Water Screes, which fall 500m straight into the deepest lake in England. Grassy and gentle from behind, spectacular at the edge.

items.title: Scafell
items.description: Scafell Pike's separate and quieter neighbour at 964m. The direct link across Mickledore is blocked by Broad Stand, a rock climb — the walkers' ways round are Lord's Rake or the Foxes Tarn gully, both loose and both requiring care.

items.title: Yewbarrow
items.description: A 628m ridge above Wasdale with steep ends at both extremities.

items.title: Haycock
items.description: A 797m remote top on the western fells above Ennerdale.

items.title: Kirk Fell
items.description: An 802m fell between Great Gable and Pillar, with steep grass on the Wasdale side.

items.title: Lingmell
items.description: An 800m shoulder of Scafell Pike with a tremendous view of the Gable and down Wasdale — often walked over without being noticed.

items.title: Great Gable
items.description: The 899m fell on the Lake District National Park emblem, with the war memorial of the Fell and Rock Climbing Club on its summit rocks. Steep on every side; the usual line from Styhead is the Breast Route.

items.title: Green Gable
items.description: An 801m top separated from Great Gable by Windy Gap, with the best close view of the parent fell.

items.title: Seathwaite Fell
items.description: A 632m knobbly fell of small tarns above Sprinkling Tarn.

items.title: Scafell Pike
items.description: England's highest ground at 978m. A boulder-strewn summit plateau with a huge cairn; cairned throughout but genuinely serious in mist, where the plateau defeats casual navigation. Usual approach from the route is via Lingmell Col.

items.title: Great End
items.description: The 910m northern buttress of the Scafell massif, with deep gullies holding snow late. Easily reached from Esk Hause and often missed by people hurrying to the Pike.

items.title: Allen Crags
items.description: A 785m top on the Esk Hause crossing, an easy addition to a Scafell day.

items.title: Esk Pike
items.description: An 885m rocky top between Bowfell and Great End, on the Esk Hause crossing.

items.title: Bowfell
items.description: A 902m pyramid at the head of Langdale with a genuinely rocky top and the Great Slab on its flank. The Band gives a long but never technical ascent.

items.title: Crinkle Crags
items.description: A 859m switchback of five distinct tops. The Bad Step on the second crinkle is a short awkward scramble — it can be bypassed on the west. Confusing ground in cloud.

items.title: Rossett Pike
items.description: A 651m top above Rossett Gill and Angle Tarn at the head of Langdale.

items.title: Pike o’ Blisco
items.description: A 705m top with two rocky summits and an outstanding view of the Crinkles.

items.title: Harrison Stickle
items.description: The highest of the Langdale Pikes at 736m, an abrupt rocky top with the whole valley beneath it.

items.title: Pavey Ark
items.description: A 700m crag above Stickle Tarn, crossed by Jack's Rake — a rising Grade 1 scramble up the face of the cliff that is exposed, polished and unforgiving when wet. The summit is reached easily from behind if the Rake is not wanted.

items.title: Pike o’ Stickle
items.description: A 709m rock thumb above Mickleden, with a neolithic axe factory in the scree below its summit.

items.title: Loft Crag
items.description: A 682m Langdale Pike above Gimmer Crag.

items.title: Sergeant Man
items.description: A 736m rocky knoll on the shoulder of High Raise, more distinct than its parent.

items.title: High Raise (Langdale)
items.description: At 762m the geographical centre of the Lake District, a broad grassy dome with a wide view.

items.title: Glaramara
items.description: A 783m ridge of rocky knolls and small tarns above Borrowdale.

items.title: Sergeant’s Crag
items.description: A 574m crag above Langstrath, next to Eagle Crag.

items.title: Eagle Crag
items.description: A 521m crag standing proud at the fork of Langstrath and Greenup — far more imposing than its height.

items.title: Ullscarf
items.description: A 726m watershed fell between Borrowdale and Thirlmere; wet underfoot and quiet.

items.title: Grange Fell
items.description: A 415m fell of wooded knolls in Borrowdale, with King's How as its finest top.

items.title: Castle Crag
items.description: The only fell under 1000ft in the Wainwrights, at 290m. A quarried knoll in the Jaws of Borrowdale with a war memorial on top and a slate-spoil path.

items.title: Maiden Moor
items.description: A 576m top continuing the Cat Bells ridge southward.

items.title: High Spy
items.description: A 653m fell along the crag edge above the Jaws of Borrowdale.

items.title: Base Brown
items.description: A 646m fell above Seathwaite with a steep nose and the Hanging Stone.

items.title: Dale Head
items.description: A 753m fell above Honister with a tall slate summit cairn and a fine view down Newlands.

items.title: Grey Knotts
items.description: A 697m rocky top directly above Honister Pass.

items.title: Brandreth
items.description: A 715m broad top on the Honister to Gable ridge.

items.title: Fleetwith Pike
items.description: A 648m fell whose nose rises straight from Gatesgarth at the head of Buttermere. Steep, direct, and a superb viewpoint down the valley.

items.title: Haystacks
items.description: At 597m, Wainwright's favourite fell and where his ashes were scattered. A knot of small tops, tarns and rock — far more interesting than its modest height suggests.

items.title: Hindscarth
items.description: A 727m fell with a long northern ridge into the Newlands valley.

items.title: Robinson
items.description: A 737m fell of rocky shelves at the western end of the Newlands ridge.

items.title: Pillar
items.description: An 892m fell above Ennerdale, best known for Pillar Rock on its northern face — a true rock climb, not a walk. The summit itself is reached easily from Black Sail Pass.

items.title: High Stile
items.description: The high point of the Buttermere ridge at 807m, looking straight down into the corrie above Bleaberry Tarn.

items.title: Whiteless Pike
items.description: A 660m peaked top on the ridge above Crummock Water.

items.title: Red Pike (Buttermere)
items.description: A 755m top of red syenite screes above Bleaberry Tarn.

items.title: Starling Dodd
items.description: A 633m grassy top on the high ridge above Ennerdale.

items.title: Great Borne
items.description: A 616m fell at the western end of the Ennerdale ridge.

items.title: Rannerdale Knotts
items.description: A 355m rocky ridge above Crummock, famous for the bluebells that fill its valley in spring.

items.title: Mellbreak
items.description: A 512m fell rising abruptly and independently from the shore of Crummock Water.

items.title: Hen Comb
items.description: A 509m isolated fell reached across marshy ground near Loweswater.

items.title: Blake Fell
items.description: A 573m high point of the Loweswater fells.

items.title: Low Fell
items.description: A 423m fell with one of the best views of the Buttermere valley.

items.title: Fellbarrow
items.description: A 416m grassy top on the north-western fringe.

items.title: Grasmoor
items.description: At 852m the highest of the north-western fells, a broad whaleback above Crummock.

items.title: Hopegill Head
items.description: A 770m summit at the head of Hobcarton Crag, one of the sharpest tops here.

items.title: Crag Hill
items.description: An 839m hub of the Coledale fells with a trig point and steep drops north.

items.title: Knott Rigg
items.description: A 556m ridge walk from the top of Newlands Hause, little visited.

items.title: Sail
items.description: A 773m top reached by an engineered zigzag path on the Coledale ridge.

items.title: Ard Crags
items.description: A 581m narrow grassy ridge above the Newlands valley.

items.title: Causey Pike
items.description: A 637m fell with an unmistakable knobbly summit and a short scramble to reach it.

items.title: Outerside
items.description: A 568m fell tucked below the Coledale ridge, usually bypassed.

items.title: Grisedale Pike
items.description: A 791m fell with a sharp profile above Braithwaite and a long ridge approach.

items.title: Lord’s Seat
items.description: A 552m high point of the Whinlatter fells, among forestry.

items.title: Barf
items.description: A 468m fell with a very steep scree face above Bassenthwaite.

items.title: Carl Side
items.description: A 746m top on the Longside ridge approach to Skiddaw.

items.title: Long Side
items.description: A 734m top on the finest ridge approach to Skiddaw.

items.title: Dodd
items.description: A 502m forested cone below Skiddaw with a cleared summit viewpoint.

items.title: Skiddaw Little Man
items.description: An 865m subsidiary top of Skiddaw with a better view than its parent.

items.title: Lonscale Fell
items.description: A 715m eastern outlier of Skiddaw with an abrupt edge above the Glenderaterra.

items.title: Latrigg
items.description: A 368m grassy hill directly above Keswick, with the best low-level view of Derwent Water and Borrowdale on the whole route.

items.title: Cat Bells
items.description: A 451m ridge above Derwent Water, out of all proportion in popularity to its size — a short, rocky, thoroughly enjoyable up-and-down with a superb view over the lake.

items.title: High Seat
items.description: A 608m top on notoriously wet ground on the Central Ridge.

items.title: Bleaberry Fell
items.description: A 590m rocky top on the ridge above Keswick.

items.title: Walla Crag
items.description: A 379m crag-edge above Derwent Water, minutes from the route.

items.title: Blencathra
items.description: An 868m fell with a superb north-eastern approach by Sharp Edge — a narrow, genuinely exposed Grade 1 arete that has caused many accidents and should be avoided when wet or windy. Scales Fell gives a straightforward alternative both up and down.

items.title: Clough Head
items.description: A 726m fell at the north end of the Dodds with a steep western face.

items.title: Great Dodd
items.description: An 857m grassy dome at the northern end of the Helvellyn range.

items.title: Sheffield Pike
items.description: A 675m fell between Glencoyne and Glenridding, above old lead workings.

items.title: Stybarrow Dodd
items.description: An 843m grassy top on the northern Helvellyn ridge.

items.title: Raise
items.description: An 883m fell holding the Lake District Ski Club tow on its northern slope.

items.title: White Side
items.description: An 863m top on the main Helvellyn ridge, easily added.

items.title: Helvellyn
items.description: At 950m, the most-climbed high fell in the district, with a summit shelter and trig point. Approaching by Striding Edge and leaving by Swirral Edge is the classic round: both are Grade 1 scrambles with real exposure, and neither is sensible in high wind, ice or poor visibility.

items.title: Catstye Cam
items.description: A sharply conical 890m top just north of Helvellyn, often bypassed entirely despite being ten minutes off Swirral Edge.

items.title: Nethermost Pike
items.description: An 891m top immediately south of Helvellyn with a fine eastern edge, usually ignored.

items.title: Birkhouse Moor
items.description: A 718m shoulder crossed on the way to Striding Edge, with the Hole-in-the-Wall on it.

items.title: Glenridding Dodd
items.description: A 442m small top above Glenridding with a good Ullswater view.

items.title: Dollywaggon Pike
items.description: An 858m top at the southern end of the Helvellyn ridge above Grisedale Tarn.

items.title: St Sunday Crag
items.description: An 841m fell with a long elegant ridge and the finest view of Helvellyn's eastern corries from across Grisedale.

items.title: Place Fell
items.description: A 657m fell above Ullswater with a knobbly top and a superb lake view.

items.title: Beda Fell
items.description: A 509m narrow ridge in Martindale, one of the quietest corners of the district.

items.title: Angletarn Pikes
items.description: A 567m twin-topped fell beside Angle Tarn, one of the prettiest small tops here.

items.title: Hart Crag
items.description: An 822m rocky top on the Fairfield horseshoe.

items.title: Hartsop Dodd
items.description: A 618m steep-fronted top above Hartsop village.

items.title: Gray Crag
items.description: A 699m long flat-topped ridge above Hayeswater.

items.title: Rest Dodd
items.description: A 696m fell on the Martindale side of the High Street ridge.

items.title: High Raise (High Street)
items.description: An 802m broad top, the highest of the far eastern fells after High Street.

items.title: Rampsgill Head
items.description: A 792m top with crags falling into Rampsgill, beside Kidsty Pike.

items.title: The Knott
items.description: A 739m rounded top at a junction of ridges above Hayeswater.

items.title: Kidsty Pike
items.description: A 780m top with a neat peaked profile above Riggindale, overlooking Haweswater.

items.title: Selside Pike
items.description: A 655m fell on the eastern fringe, with a summit shelter.

items.title: Branstree
items.description: A 713m grassy fell above Haweswater with survey pillars on its flank.

items.title: High Street
items.description: An 828m whaleback carrying the line of a Roman road, with a wall along the top. Broad and easy going, and the route already crosses it.

items.title: Mardale Ill Bell
items.description: A 760m top between Nan Bield and High Street, above Blea Water.

items.title: Harter Fell (Mardale)
items.description: A 778m fell above Nan Bield Pass, with a summit cairn built partly of old iron fence posts and a fine view down Haweswater.

items.title: Thornthwaite Crag
items.description: A 784m top marked by a 4m stone beacon, at the junction of several ridges.

items.title: Stony Cove Pike
items.description: A 763m top also known as Caudale Moor, above the Kirkstone Pass.

items.title: Froswick
items.description: A 720m cone on the Kentmere horseshoe, a smaller echo of Ill Bell.

items.title: Ill Bell
items.description: The finest top on the Kentmere horseshoe at 757m, cone-shaped with three large cairns.

items.title: Red Screes
items.description: A 776m fell rising directly from the top of the Kirkstone Pass, with a summit tarn.

items.title: Yoke
items.description: A 706m fell with Rainsborrow Crag on its Kentmere flank.

items.title: Sallows
items.description: A 516m grassy fell on the Kentmere fringe.

items.title: Sour Howes
items.description: A 483m undulating fell above Troutbeck.

items.title: Dove Crag
items.description: A 792m fell with a fine crag and the Priest's Hole cave beneath it.

items.title: Loughrigg Fell
items.description: A 335m maze of little tops, tarns and caves between Grasmere and Ambleside — much more rambling than its height suggests.

items.title: Heron Pike
items.description: A 612m top on the Rydal side of the Fairfield horseshoe.

items.title: Seat Sandal
items.description: A 736m fell above Grisedale Tarn and Dunmail Raise.

items.title: Fairfield
items.description: An 873m fell with a broad flat summit plateau that is confusing in cloud — the drops on the north side are abrupt.

items.title: Great Rigg
items.description: A 766m top on the Fairfield horseshoe above Rydal.

items.title: Silver How
items.description: A 395m top above Grasmere with a fine view of the vale and the Langdale Pikes.

items.title: Blea Rigg
items.description: A 541m ridge of knolls between Easedale and Langdale.

items.title: Lingmoor Fell
items.description: A 469m ridge between the two Langdales, with old slate quarries and a first-rate view of the Pikes.

items.title: Black Fell
items.description: A 323m top with a National Trust monument column and a wide low-level view.

items.title: Holme Fell
items.description: A 317m knot of rock and old quarries with a view down Yewdale.

items.title: Wetherlam
items.description: A 762m fell riddled with old mine levels and shafts on its southern flanks — stay on the paths.

items.title: Swirl How
items.description: An 802m hub of the Coniston fells, reached from Levers Hause or the Prison Band.

items.title: Great Carrs
items.description: A 785m top with the wreckage of a wartime Halifax bomber on the col below its summit.

items.title: Grey Friar
items.description: A 773m western outlier of the Coniston fells, looking over the Duddon.

items.title: Brim Fell
items.description: A 796m grassy top on the ridge north of Coniston Old Man.

items.title: Coniston Old Man
items.description: An 803m fell rising straight from the village, its flanks full of slate quarries and copper workings. Large summit cairn and a view to the sea.

items.title: Dow Crag
items.description: A 778m summit perched above five great climbing buttresses dropping to Goats Water. The walk up is easy; the north face is not.

items.title: Harter Fell (Eskdale)
items.description: A 653m fell of rocky tors above Eskdale, and one of the best-shaped small fells in the district. The true summit needs a short easy scramble.

items.title: Cold Pike
items.description: A 701m top of three rocky summits beside the Crinkles.

items.title: Hard Knott
items.description: A 549m rocky fell above the pass, with the remains of the Roman fort of Mediobogdum on its shoulder.

items.title: Green Crag
items.description: A 489m rocky tor on the Eskdale moors, rarely visited.
